body_long:
Hilton publishes its third-quarter 2026 results on Tuesday 27 October, before the US market opens, with a conference call at 9 a.m. Eastern time.

## Where Hilton stood after the second quarter

In July, Hilton raised its full-year forecast for room revenue growth on the back of strong demand for its luxury hotels. The second quarter also showed the weight of the regional conflict on the Gulf: Hilton's room revenue in the Middle East and Africa fell 29.5% over the period.

## What to watch

Three points will matter for our audience. First, the gap between luxury and the rest of the portfolio: Waldorf Astoria, Conrad and LXR have been the strongest part of Hilton's growth. Second, the Middle East: Accor reported a clear improvement in the UAE in the third quarter, and Hilton's figures will show whether that recovery is shared. Third, development: the pace of signings and conversions in Europe, where Hilton has been expanding its luxury and lifestyle brands.

## The signal

The third-quarter season so far points in one direction. Accor reported luxury RevPAR up 8.9% and IHG global RevPAR up 5.3%, with Europe resilient and the Gulf improving. Hilton's figures will confirm, or nuance, that picture for the largest US luxury portfolios.

We will publish the key figures once the results are out.
